findings.title: .custom-message-length light-theme color silently changed from 70% to 30% lightness
findings.body: The original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The replacement puts `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` in the light-theme slot of dark-light-choose, so the light theme now gets a much darker text color. The PR is meant to add a dark-theme fallback, not change light-theme output, so this is an unrelated visual regression for every light-theme user.

findings.title: .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a light-theme color changed from 30% to 70% lightness
findings.body: The diff replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), ...)`. The light-theme value jumps from 30% to 70% lightness, so the link becomes far lighter than before on light themes. The dark-theme fallback is the only change the PR title describes, so this is an unintended regression.

findings.title: .topic-map h3 light-theme color changed from 20% to 50% lightness
findings.body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new value uses 50% for the light theme and 50% for the dark theme (`scale-color($secondary, 50%)`), which changes the light-theme heading color and drops the intended dark-theme 80% fallback. Neither part matches the PR's stated purpose.

findings.title: .group-member-info .name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
findings.body: The original used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new dark-light-choose call uses 50% for the light theme, which changes the existing light-theme output. This is not a dark-theme fix.

findings.title: .group-member-info .name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
findings.body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` for the light theme, so the light-theme name color is altered without being mentioned in the PR title or description.

findings.title: No verification or description for a broad theme-color change across 32 files
findings.body: The PR touches about 80 color declarations across 32 stylesheets, but the description is just 'Test 7' and no visual or compile check is described. Several hunks alter light-theme values (see the other findings), so a reviewer cannot tell which changes are intended without a before/after review of both themes.
